subject: UniProtKB:G3XCX1
description: Gene-product component of the Nar respiratory ensemble, not isolated-subunit catalysis. Current activity is ARBA inference; the source vectorial proton convention is not derived from that chemical-class annotation.

evidence.source_assertion: This current UniProtKB unreviewed (TrEMBL) entry assigns G3XCX1 to taxon 208964, narG / PA3875, with a 1261-residue sequence. It does not establish sequence identity to every historical preparation.

subject: UniProtKB:Q59647
description: Subunit function in the NorBC ensemble, not isolated-subunit catalysis. Current NorB proton-pump prose is excluded. RCSB 3O0R PAO1 preparations differ from current sequences (NorB lacks current R301; NorC K100 versus N100), so no exact construct equivalence is asserted.

evidence.source_assertion: This current UniProtKB reviewed (Swiss-Prot) entry assigns Q59647 to taxon 208964, norB / PA0524, with a 466-residue sequence. It does not establish sequence identity to every historical preparation.
The reviewed entry describes a heterodimer consisting of a large cytochrome b subunit and a small cytochrome c subunit.
The catalytic annotation is Rhea 30211, a cytochrome-c NO/N2O reaction class; reduction proceeds in its reverse direction.
The primary abstract reports a P. aeruginosa NOR structure, an FeB center with three His and one Glu ligands, and no D- or K-proton pathway; extracellular proton delivery is proposed.
The mmCIF assigns entity 3, NorB, a 465-residue sequence and natural PAO1 source.
The inferred FUNCTION annotation (ECO:0000250) states proton-pump activity. This source statement is retained as a conflict and is not adopted as a transport or energy-coupling assertion.
The structural discussion states that no obvious D/K proton-pumping channel or hydrogen-bond network connects cytoplasm and periplasm, consistent with cNOR lacking proton-pumping ability.

subject: UniProtKB:Q9HYL2
description: NosZ activity is annotated by HAMAP; PAO1 deletion physiology independently supports terminal N2O reduction. Generic c-type electron donor is a source reaction convention, not a uniquely identified physiological partner.

evidence.source_assertion: This current UniProtKB reviewed (Swiss-Prot) entry assigns Q9HYL2 to taxon 208964, nosZ / PA3392, with a 636-residue sequence. It does not establish sequence identity to every historical preparation.
The entry assigns nitrous-oxide reductase activity (Rhea 43108) using ECO:0000255 HAMAP-Rule MF_00716.
The PAO1 nosZ deletion strain accumulates N2O during denitrification; NosZ loss is the engineered physiological block.
The nosZ mutant accumulates N2O under anoxia, whereas wild-type PAO1 produces less than 10 micromolar N2O under the experimental nitrate concentrations.
